exercise.name: Cable Seated Reverse Fly

reference.title: Cable Seated Reverse Fly (male)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

equipment: Cable crossover (two pulleys at shoulder height)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the arms open out to the sides, breathe in as they come back together.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s out, short pause, about 2 s back

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack loads are user-chosen and light: pick a weight you can open with soft, unchanging elbows and no shrug.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then a plate on each stack; add a 1 s hold out wide

cues.text: Sit tall on the seat between two pulleys set at shoulder height; hold the left cable in the right hand and the right cable in the left, arms long in front at shoulder height, thumbs up, elbows soft.
Breathe out and sweep the arms out to the sides in a wide arc, keeping the elbows softly bent and the hands at shoulder height.
Arms in a T, in line with the shoulders; shoulders down, chest tall.
Breathe in and let the arms come back together in front under control.
Brief pause with the hands in front, then open again.

mistakes.mistake: Bending and straightening the elbows (turning it into a row)
mistakes.fix: Lock the elbows at a soft bend; the movement is only at the shoulders.
Keep the shoulders down and away from the ears; lighten the load.

mistakes.mistake: Swinging the arms back past the body
mistakes.fix: Stop when the arms are in line with the shoulders.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to move the weight
mistakes.fix: Sit tall and keep the trunk still.

kinematics.norm: From arms in front to arms in line with the shoulders (clinical opinion); in a horizontal abduction exercise the posterior deltoid was highly active and hand position changed its activity (Schoenfeld 2013)
Arms near shoulder height throughout (clinical opinion)
Soft and unchanged, about 10-20 degrees (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s out and 2 s back (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Seated Reverse Fly (male), video (movement reference)
Schoenfeld et al. 2013, effect of hand position on EMG activity of the posterior shoulder musculature during a horizontal abduction exercise (J Strength Cond Res 27(10):2644-2649)
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain at the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable loads are user-chosen: rear-deltoid work needs light loads to keep the elbows soft and the shoulders down.
At the end of the set bring the hands together in front and let the cables back to the stacks slowly.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: open only to about 45 degrees short of the T, or lower the pulleys a little below shoulder height (clinical opinion).
No crossover machine: band pull-apart or a seated dumbbell reverse fly.
